newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell to 1.597 billion yuan from 1.7 billion yuan on Sunday with the 120-day contract the most actively traded.
Trading remained slow on Monday with the state-run banks remaining on the sidelines, traders said.
"The state-run banks have ample money supply at present due to surging bank deposits," one trader said. "So they are reluctant to trade on the market."
Traders said non-banking financial institutions including securities houses were the most active traders trading through the short-term financial centres, money brokerages run by the central bank.
The surge on the domestic A share market today was the major factor fanning fund demand, they added.
Traders said they expect the rates to stick around current levels in the short-term.
